Where design meets working code

I’m Arun, a developer who lives in the space between a designer’s file and a product people actually use. I care about the details that make an interface feel right: spacing that’s consistent, layouts that hold up on every screen size, and interactions that respond the way people expect.

My career actually started as an office admin. I taught myself UI development, and that’s where my developer journey began. Along the way, project requirements led me to Angular, then React and Next.js, and then to Flutter, so today I build for the web and for mobile. I also enjoy the foundations other developers build on: component libraries in Angular and React, and design system style packages published to npm, so teams ship consistent UI without reinventing it.

At CareStack I work as a Senior Software Engineer on software used every day by dental practices. Outside work, I’m a fitness enthusiast and a table tennis player, and I’m a little crazy about driving heavy vehicles like buses and trucks. I also enjoy building small tools, like the editor extensions below.

What I do

UI development

Responsive, accessible interfaces built with clean HTML, CSS and JavaScript that match the design down to the pixel.

Flutter apps

Cross-platform mobile apps in Flutter and Dart, with smooth animations and a consistent look on Android and iOS, including a B2B app for dental providers.

Angular and React

Full Angular projects, not just components, plus reusable component libraries in both Angular and React, and Next.js work too.

Design to code

Close collaboration with designers to turn mockups into production-ready screens without losing the intent.

Design system on npm

CSS style packages for design systems, published to npm so every team installs the same tokens, utilities and components. The one I built has 33 components and is used by every developer on our main product.

AI-assisted UI

Claude skills connected to Figma through MCP that turn designs, screenshots and prototypes into Angular components that follow our design system.

Things I’ve built for developers
An AI skill that turns designs into Angular code, and four extensions for VS Code, Antigravity, Cursor and other editors. Try them right here.
Claude skill + Figma MCP
CareFlow Skill: design to Angular
Figma links, screenshots or prototypes in, production-ready Angular out
A Claude skill I built around our design system. Paste a Figma link and it connects through the Figma MCP server, reads the frames and splits the screen into Angular components that follow the Figma structure. It works from a screenshot or an HTML prototype too.
  • Uses only the design system’s own component, utility and icon classes, and never invents one
  • No inline styles, no custom CSS, no outside UI frameworks
  • Plans first: shows a blueprint and confirms scope before writing code
  • Uses the shared Angular component library when it’s installed, with a CSS-only fallback when it isn’t
  • Asks the developer instead of guessing, including before installing any package
  • Claude
  • Figma MCP
  • Angular
  • Design system on npm
  
input › figma.com/design/…/Schedule?node-id=12-48
  1. Fetch frames and tokens through Figma MCP
  2. Plan the screen and draft a blueprint
  3. Confirm scope with the developer
  4. Map every element to cfc-* and cfu-* classes
  5. Generate Angular components and templates

CareFlow Styleguide
The whole design system, inside the editor
Browse the CareFlow design system from a tree in the VS Code sidebar. Pick any style or component to see a live preview with its neatly formatted code underneath, ready to copy. It also adds snippets for utility classes and component templates, and click-to-copy icons. Hover the boxes below: each one uses its own cursor class.
